audit_findings.title: Tax-group liability could create a claim far beyond CIX’s own tax expense
audit_findings.mechanism: A payment for another Contran Tax Group member would reduce cash or create an equity-bridge liability; recurring assessments could also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Under applicable law, we, as well as every other member of the Contran Tax Group, are each jointly and severally liable for the aggregate federal income tax liability of Contran and the other companies included in the Contran Tax Group for all periods in which we are included in the Contran Tax Group.
audit_findings.explanation: Joint-and-several liability is demonstrated, but no unpaid group exposure or probable CIX payment is established. NL’s indemnity mitigates the risk, although its enforceability and credit support are untested. The record therefore cannot establish whether the exposure is large enough to alter the $20.45–$25.62 per-share valuation range.
audit_findings.action: Quantify exposures for every open tax year and obtain the tax-sharing agreement, NL credit analysis, indemnity-enforcement analysis, and any tax authority claims; deduct any probability-weighted uncovered amount in a bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: PFAS litigation is an unmodeled contingent cash claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Defense costs, settlement, or judgment would reduce OE or cash available in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2024, we were served with four lawsuits by public water companies in South Carolina that seek recovery of future costs to remove perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (known as “PFAS”) from their water supplies.
audit_findings.explanation: The four lawsuits are demonstrated, but liability and damages are not. The latest 10-Q records no accrual because liability is uncertain and cannot be reasonably estimated, while management currently expects no material adverse effect. That does not resolve uninsured defense costs or tail exposure, so materiality remains unestablished.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current pleadings, allocation theories, claimed remediation costs, defense-cost history, insurance and indemnity coverage, counsel’s loss range, and subsequent case developments; rerun with a probability-weighted deduction if supportable.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains a disclosed one-time stocking benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.7 million of sales; associated OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrecurring after-tax contribution embedded in FY2025 OE is capitalized through the DCF anchor and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Marine Components net sales increased 22% in 2025 as compared to 2024 primarily due to $2.7 million higher sales to the towboat market (including a one-time stocking event for a towboat OEM customer), $2.5 million higher sales to the government market and $2.2 million higher sales to the industrial market, partially offset by $1.1 million lower sales to the center console market.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring sale is demonstrated, but its profit contribution is not disclosed. As a conservative scale test, removing the entire $2.7 million sales amount from OE would reduce indicated value by approximately $2.61–$3.44 per share across the scenarios; even adjusted bull value would be about $22.18 per share versus the $35 market price. The valuation conclusion therefore would not change, and the actual effect must be smaller than this full-revenue sensitivity absent secondary effects.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the event’s gross profit, incremental operating costs, tax effect, and working-capital impact; normalize FY2025 OE by the actual after-tax contribution in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: A non-operating affiliate receivable may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.8 million at June 30, 2026, equal to approximately $0.55 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The principal is a non-operating asset whose interest income was purged from OE, so its collectible value belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The outstanding principal amount of the note receivable from affiliate of $8.0 million at December 31, 2025 bears interest at prime plus 1.0% (7.8% at December 31, 2025).
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that the separately reported affiliate note remained outstanding at $6.8 million, while the bridge includes only $52.421 million of cash and no amount for the note. Adding it at full par would raise values to approximately $21.00, $23.93, and $26.17 per share—still below the $35 price—so it does not change the conclusion. Related-party and unsecured credit risk could make the addition smaller.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the note was not included in another bridge line, assess Valhi’s repayment capacity and post-quarter collections, then rerun the bridge using its risk-adjusted collectible principal.

audit_findings.title: Forward capital requirements exceed the anchor-year spending level
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 forecast of $5.5 million, $1.8 million above FY2025 capital expenditures of $3.7 million
audit_findings.mechanism: A sustainable increase in maintenance capital would reduce forecast OE; capacity or growth capital should instead be assessed against the growth it supports.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our capital expenditures in 2026 to total approximately $4.3 million, primarily to support expected customer demand and to maintain and improve our facilities and technology infrastructure.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest forecast has increased from $4.3 million to $5.5 million, but the filing says spending is primarily for capacity, new technology, automation, and facility improvements. The record does not establish that the $1.8 million increase is recurring maintenance capital, and it is not part of the FY2025 actual anchor. It is therefore a forward-looking item to monitor rather than a demonstrated anchor error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level maintenance-versus-expansion classifications, actual 2026 spending, expected useful lives, and incremental earnings; rerun sustainable OE if recurring maintenance exceeds $3.7 million.

audit_findings.title: Shared insurance can transmit affiliate losses to CIX
audit_findings.mechanism: An assessment under the loss-sharing agreement would reduce cash or OE and could require an equity-bridge liability.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, and in the event that the available coverage under a particular policy would become exhausted by one or more claims, Contran and certain of its subsidiaries and affiliates, including us, have entered into a loss sharing agreement under which any uninsured loss arising because the available coverage had been exhausted by one or more claims will be shared ratably amongst those entities that had submitted claims under the relevant policy.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual loss-sharing mechanism is demonstrated, but no policy exhaustion, affiliate loss, assessment, or maximum exposure is supplied. Historical insurance-program payments do not cap this contingent obligation. The possibility may affect value, but the current record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Review the agreement’s allocation formula, policy limits, aggregate claims, participating entities, historical assessments, reinsurance recoverability, and maximum reasonably possible CIX share; model a deduction if a supportable exposure emerges.
